notes:
I only got third-party listings, not the venues' own hours pages, so I left `when` and `price` out of every pick. Search ran out before I could open the operators' pages.

```json
{
  "picks": [
    {
      "name": "Canadian Children's Museum, Canadian Museum of History (100 Laurier St, Gatineau)",
      "age_fit": "3-8 years",
      "source_name": "Canadian Museum of History"
    },
    {
      "name": "ZOOOM - Children's Innovation Zone, Canada Science and Technology Museum (1867 St. Laurent Blvd, Ottawa)",
      "age_fit": "Children's Innovation Zone",
      "source_name": "Ingenium"
    },
    {
      "name": "Canadian Museum of Nature (240 McLeod St, Ottawa)",
      "age_fit": "Child, ages 3-12 (kindergarten - grade 6)",
      "source_name": "Canadian Museum of Nature"
    }
  ]
}
```

What the search showed for each pick:
- **Canadian Children's Museum:** 
One admission covers both the Children's Museum and the Canadian Museum of History.
 
The ideal age is 3-8 years, with hands-on, imaginative play.
 It is in Gatineau, Quebec, just across the river from Ottawa. The only hours I saw were on listing sites, which showed 9-5 with a late night on Thursdays.
- **Canada Science and Technology Museum:** 
It has ZOOOM – Children's Innovation Zone and a tinker lab called Exploratek.
 The hours I saw came from listing sites. They disagreed on whether Mondays are open, so I left `when` out.
- **Canadian Museum of Nature:** Its own page lists a child admission category for 
ages 3-12, kindergarten to grade 6
. That page is the group-visits page, so it gives no hours for a family visit. Listing sites gave closing times of 4, 5 or 6 pm and disagreed on whether Tuesdays are closed, so I left `when` out.

Gaps:
- I found no zoo, aquarium or playground with a source I could cite, so none are in the list.
- The window "August 30 to September 2" has no year. Today is October 15, 2026, so it likely means 2027, and nothing I read covers those dates.
- Free-admission offers for children that I saw were tied to a 2026 federal pass, so I did not treat them as applying to the window.
